Harbor Yoga — fictional business brief for demonstration

Services: Harbor Yoga offers beginner yoga classes for adults in the local neighborhood. Introductory classes require advance booking. Each class has a maximum capacity of twelve participants.

Audience: First-time adult students who prefer calm instruction and an approachable environment. Many prospects feel intimidated by unfamiliar poses. They want to understand what to expect before booking.

Brand voice: Warm, clear, welcoming, and practical. Explain the experience without promising health benefits.

Restrictions: Do not advertise discounts or guaranteed health outcomes. Prices are not provided in this brief. Instructor availability for video filming has not been confirmed. No testimonials or previous campaign results have been supplied.

Goal context: We want to increase introductory bookings while staying within our class capacity. Useful experiments could compare explanations of a first visit with introductions to the teaching approach. These are proposed experiments, not proven results.
input.goal: Recommend the next experiment using our recorded results

cases.expected: Use the supplied source-labeled metrics; no fabricated performance or causal claims.

retrieval_checks.query: How can first-time visitors learn what to expect in a class?

actual.text: Operations handbook: expense reimbursement requests require an invoice and a manager signature. Submit invoices by the last business day each month. This handbook does not contain audience research or class descriptions.

ideas.title: Compare first visit explanations with teaching approach introductions
ideas.rationale: The business goal is to increase introductory bookings while staying within class capacity. The current results show Instagram leads are higher than Facebook leads, but both channels have low conversion rates. The brief suggests experiments comparing explanations of a first visit with introductions to the teaching approach to address prospect intimidation.
ideas.audience: First-time adult students who prefer calm instruction and an approachable environment. Many prospects feel intimidated by unfamiliar poses and want to understand what to expect before booking.

supporting_facts.claim: The business aims to increase introductory bookings without exceeding class capacity
supporting_facts.quote: We want to increase introductory bookings while staying within our class capacity.

supporting_facts.claim: Prospects feel intimidated by unfamiliar poses and need clarity on expectations
supporting_facts.quote: Many prospects feel intimidated by unfamiliar poses. They want to understand what to expect before booking.

proposed_actions: Run A/B test on Instagram ads comparing two ad variants: one explaining the first visit experience (e.g., 'Your first class: 15-minute intro session with a friendly instructor') vs. one introducing the teaching approach (e.g., 'How we guide you through poses safely')
Track conversion rates for each variant to measure which explanation reduces intimidation and increases bookings
Ensure ad variants comply with brand voice: warm, clear, welcoming, and practical without promising health benefits
Use Instagram's A/B testing feature to run the test within the 2026-12-20 deadline
assumptions: Instagram's A/B testing feature is available for the business
The teaching approach explanation will be more effective than the first visit explanation for reducing intimidation
The business has sufficient class capacity to accommodate increased bookings without exceeding twelve participants per class
success_metrics: Higher conversion rate from Instagram ads (leads to class bookings) compared to current baseline
Increased number of first-time students booking introductory classes without feeling intimidated
Maintaining class capacity at twelve participants per class
risks: Ad variants may not significantly impact booking rates due to low conversion rates in current results
Instructor availability for video filming may limit ad production
The business may not have enough class capacity to handle increased bookings
